newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales rose in Sept from yr ago -report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales rose in Sept from yr ago -report.

text.p: Closed escrow sales of California detached homes increased during September from a year ago, but declined slightly from August, according to a report released on Friday.

The California Association of Realtors and Transamerica's MetroScan real estate service said median home prices increased during September from a year ago in 152 of the more than 300 selected California cities and areas.
"We have now seen one continuous year of statewide sales increases on a monthly basis, compared with the year before," said California Association of Realtors President Rick Snyder.

Statewide, 512,620 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow during September on a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis, down 2.8 percent from a revised annualized rate of 527,460 homes sold in August.

The September sales pace jumped 12.2 percent from the September 1995 annualized rate, when 456,920 homes were sold. Year-to-date, statewide home sales have increased 23.2 percent, compared with the January through September period in 1995, according to the report.

The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during September was $179,630, down 0.7 percent from $180,830 in August. The September median price edged down 0.5 percent from September 1995, when the median-priced home sold for $180,530, the report said.

Fixed mortgage interest rates averaged 8.23 percent during September, up from an average of 7.95 percent in August and 7.61 percent in September 1995, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. Adjustable mortgage interest rates averaged 5.85 percent in September, up slightly from 5.81 percent in August and 5.80 percent in September 1995.
